name: Phase 3 extension model: prompt templates, skills, theme files, hooks, MCP prompts (E0 + E1 + E2)
description: E0 resources (resources.rs, tui/theme.rs): prompts/<name>.md become /<name> with frontmatter description and argument-hint, $1..$9, $@/$ARGUMENTS and ${1:-default} filled from shell-split arguments (unused arguments are appended, not dropped); Agent Skills SKILL.md folders under ~/.rusti/skills, ~/.agents/skills and, once trusted, .rusti/skills and .agents/skills, listed by name, description and absolute path in the system prompt (disable-model-invocation keeps one off), /skill:name args sends the body in a <skill> block; themes/<name>.json in rusti's 16 colour roles plus fail/ask tints, #rrggbb or raw SGR, inheriting from a base (built-in or an earlier theme file), joining /themes, the active file hot-reloaded by mtime about once a second. The / menu is built-ins, then templates, then skills, then MCP prompts, tagged [u]/[p]/[mcp:server]; a built-in wins a name collision with a warning; it is re-read whenever a lone / opens it. E1 hooks (ai_core/hooks.rs, config.json "hooks"): user_shell (F09: rewrite, handle or block a ! command), pre_tool (after the permission gate, args rewrite or block), post_tool (redact), user_prompt (rewrite or block, steers too), session_start (context on the session's first message this run), pre_compact (own summary or skip); JSON on stdin, a JSON decision on stdout, per-hook timeout, chained in config order; failure blocks where blocking means something, withholds post_tool output, and is only reported for session_start. E2 (ai_core/mcp.rs): a server advertising prompts gets /<server>:<prompt> args, words mapped onto the declared arguments in order (the last takes the rest), fetched with prompts/get on the agent thread and sent as the user message. The trust gate also covers ./.agents/skills.
evidence: cargo test (84 unit tests + the trust e2e): resources::tests frontmatter_reads_the_yaml_subset_skills_use, arguments_split_like_a_shell, template_placeholders_expand (the captain's /review example), templates_and_skills_load_with_user_first; ai_core::hooks::tests::hook_decisions_chain_block_and_fail_safe (rewrite chain, handled, block, exit/timeout/non-object failures, pre_tool rewrite and refusal, post_tool redaction and withheld output, user_prompt, session_start, pre_compact); tui::theme::tests::theme_files_load_inherit_and_hot_reload (hex/SGR, base inheritance, tints, every error, mtime reload, broken edit keeps the last good version); ai_core::mcp::tests::talks_to_a_real_stdio_server extended with prompts/list, prompt_args and prompts/get against tests/fake_mcp_server.py; tui::tests::bang_bang_output_never_reaches_the_model extended with a refusing user_shell hook; tui::app::tests::extensions_join_the_menu_and_run_as_their_text; config trust test now covers .agents/skills. One-shot run with RUSTI_HOME holding a blocking user_prompt hook and a misspelt event: printed the unknown-event warning and 'error: message not sent: no secrets in prompts', exit 1.
decisions: Hooks are installed once at startup like the shell (hooks::set), so a test or sub-run never runs a developer's real hooks; helpers take the hook list as an argument for testing.
Hooks run in the configured shell (tools::shell), so a hook command is written like any ! command.
post_tool failing withholds the output rather than passing it through: a redaction hook that crashed must not leak what it guarded.
session_start context rides on that turn's user entry, not the system prompt, so the prompt prefix stays byte-identical for caching.
Templates and skills are re-read from disk on submit, so an edit applies with no restart; a user's own name wins over the project's so a cloned repo cannot shadow /review.
Unused template arguments are appended after a blank line instead of being dropped (Pi drops them). ${@:N:L} slices are not supported (ponytail note).
MCP prompts are fetched on the agent thread (Job::McpPrompt), so a slow server cannot freeze the UI.
Theme strings are leaked per load (Theme fields are &'static); the ponytail note records the ceiling.
